Calculation Details

MetricValueNote

How to estimate a used car's value

Use a current local retail asking price for a closely comparable vehicle, then adjust for condition, mileage, options, history, and local demand. The calculator derives separate planning ranges for dealer retail, private-party sale, and dealer trade-in.

adjusted retail = local benchmark x condition factor x regional factor + mileage adjustment + options adjustment

Used-car value example

A $22,000 local retail benchmark in good condition, adjusted down $500 for mileage, produces an adjusted retail estimate of $20,400 before any options or regional adjustment. The private-party and trade-in estimates are lower to reflect different selling channels.

Choose the right benchmark

Match year, make, model, trim, engine, drivetrain, major options, title history, mileage, and ZIP-area market as closely as possible. Asking prices are not completed sale prices, so review several listings rather than relying on one unusually high or low example.

Retail, private-party, and trade-in values

Dealer retail reflects a vehicle offered by a business. Private-party value estimates an as-is transaction between individuals. Trade-in value is typically lower because the dealer must leave room for inspection, reconditioning, inventory, and operating costs.

Vehicle condition

Most vehicles should not be rated excellent. Consider mechanical condition, warning lights, tires, glass, paint, interior wear, accident and title history, maintenance records, odors, and required repairs. Be consistent with the condition of your benchmark vehicle.

Independent comparison

This calculator has no live VIN or transaction feed. Use it to reconcile listings and offers, then compare with a professional valuation. The Kelley Blue Book value FAQ notes that age, mileage, equipment, condition, and location affect value.

Frequently asked questions

Why is the value shown as a range?

Real transactions vary with negotiation, local supply, buyer demand, inspection results, and timing. A range is more honest than false single-dollar precision.

Does the calculator know my VIN?

No. You supply the comparable market price and adjustments. Use a VIN-based valuation provider for vehicle-specific market data.

Can an accident change the estimate?

Yes. Enter a negative options and history adjustment based on comparable vehicles or documented appraisal evidence.
